skill.name: gws-calendar
skill.description: Manage Google Calendar calendars, events, ACLs, free/busy data, and settings through the gws CLI.
skill.summary: Use Google Calendar API resources and schema-aware gws commands from AI assistants.
skill.author: googleworkspace

security_audit.summary: Static findings for Ruby or shell backtick execution and path traversal are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, command examples, and relative links. The main residual risk is semantic: the skill exposes destructive Google Calendar operations that require careful confirmation and authorized credentials.

remediation.issue: Destructive calendar and ACL operations can remove events, calendars, or access rules.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to confirm the calendar, event, and ACL target before delete, clear, patch, update, or move operations.

remediation.issue: Shared prerequisite instructions are referenced through a relative parent path.
remediation.suggestion: Package or link the shared security rules in a stable marketplace-visible location so reviewers and users can inspect them easily.

content.value_statement: Calendar administration often needs precise API calls and schema-aware parameters. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code inspect and run Google Calendar commands.
actual_capabilities: Lists Google Calendar API resources and supported methods.
Uses gws calendar help output to discover command syntax.
Uses gws schema output to inspect required parameters and types.
Supports calendar, event, ACL, calendar list, color, settings, and freebusy resources.
Documents helper commands for event insertion and agenda review.
Includes watch and channel stop methods for Calendar change tracking.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Requires Google Calendar permissions for the requested account and scopes.
Does not provide a graphical calendar interface.
Destructive methods need separate user confirmation before execution.

use_cases.title: Review a busy day
use_cases.description: Inspect upcoming events and free/busy windows before scheduling new meetings.

use_cases.title: Maintain shared calendars
use_cases.description: Update calendar metadata, list calendars, and manage access rules with schema-aware commands.

use_cases.title: Automate event workflows
use_cases.description: Create, update, move, or inspect events from repeatable assistant-driven workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List my calendars
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Google Calendar skill to inspect the calendar list command. Then show the safest command to list my calendars.

prompt_templates.title: Find free time
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the freebusy resource to check availability for these calendars over this time range. Explain the parameters before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Update an event safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the schema for updating a Google Calendar event. Build the command, identify required IDs, and ask for confirmation before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit calendar permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review ACL methods for a shared calendar. List current rules, identify risky permissions, and propose exact patch commands without executing them.

output_examples.input: Show me how to list events on my primary calendar next week.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the events list method, names the required calendar ID and date filters, and provides a ready-to-review command.

output_examples.input: Create a planning meeting tomorrow afternoon.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks the insert helper or event schema, summarizes the event details, and asks for confirmation before creating it.

output_examples.input: Who can access the team calendar?
output_examples.output: The assistant uses ACL list guidance to retrieve access rules and summarizes each rule by role, scope, and potential risk.

best_practices: Inspect the schema before constructing parameters for any method.
Confirm target calendar IDs and event IDs before making changes.
Use read-only list or get methods before delete, clear, patch, or update.
anti_patterns: Running destructive methods without confirming the exact target.
Using broad credentials when a limited Google Calendar scope is enough.
Assuming imported or moved events keep every original event property.

faq.question: Does this skill require Google authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The gws CLI must be authenticated with access to the target Google Calendar data.

faq.question: Can it create and update events?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents events insert, update, patch, move, quickAdd, import, list, get, delete, and instances methods.

faq.question: Can it manage calendar permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. The ACL resource includes methods to list, get, insert, patch, update, watch, and delete access rules.

faq.question: Does it include free/busy checks?
faq.answer: Yes. The freebusy query method returns availability information for one or more calendars.

faq.question: Can it delete calendar data?
faq.answer: Yes. Some Calendar API methods can delete events, calendars, or access rules, so confirm targets before use.

faq.question: Is this a standalone calendar application?
faq.answer: No. It is a command guidance skill for the gws CLI and Google Calendar API resources.
